Questions.content: What is the side length of the original square, and how does its area change in percentage terms without specific numerical values? The TG assumes a general case but does not specify how to handle the calculation if the side length is not given numerically.

Answers.content:
The side length of the original square can be represented as \( s \).

When two opposite sides are decreased by 40%, their new lengths become \( 0.6s \). Similarly, the other two opposite sides, when increased by 50%, become \( 1.5s \).

The area of the original square is:
\[ A_{\text{original}} = s^2 \]

The area of the resulting rectangle is:
\[ A_{\text{new}} = (0.6s) \times (1.5s) = 0.9s^2 \]

To find the percentage decrease in the area, we calculate:
\[ \text{Percentage Decrease} = \left( \frac{A_{\text{original}} - A_{\text{new}}}{A_{\text{original}}} \right) \times 100 = \left( \frac{s^2 - 0.9s^2}{s^2} \right) \times 100 = (0.1) \times 100 = 10\% \]

Thus, the area of the square decreases by \( 10\% \).
